The norm difference vanishes iff sin(2t_j)=0, yielding the unique n=4 exceptional stationarity. Determinant and lattice sine bounds give an explicit phase-uniform gradient coordinate. A global bound on two incident chord length second derivatives and a finite one-coordinate perturbation produce the claimed positive gap. The full proof covers all a>b>0, n>=3 and all phase parameters. A fixed-seed 2,320-assertion verifier corroborates exact formulas, but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact all-order obstruction to simultaneous finite n-gon area/perimeter extrema in ellipses, isolating the exceptional four-vertex geometry. It does more than restate angular perimeter ordering within area maximizers: it tests independent boundary motions and gives a computable positive gap against unrestricted perimeter optimization. It is motivated by the 2026 asymptotic dual-objective rigidity question and longstanding extremal ellipse n-gon problems, without claiming a paper-sized result or a sharp coefficient.
